description: Canonical HPKE (RFC 9180) suite vocabulary for v1 application-layer public-key sealing surfaces that are NOT carried inside MLS: key-backup `recovery_public_key` envelopes, to-device sealed material (`ak.secret.send`), member-application reviewer envelopes and file-transfer key envelopes. An HPKE suite names the (KEM, KDF, AEAD) triple; its canonical_id is the wire scheme / `hpke_suite` selector value. The KEM (DHKEM-X25519-HKDF-SHA256), the KDF (HKDF-SHA256) and the application-layer seal/open transcript are standard RFC 9180 base mode (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR): the RFC 9180 key_schedule with LabeledExtract / LabeledExpand derives key, base_nonce and exporter_secret from the DHKEM shared secret and the caller `info`, and the AEAD nonce is the internally derived base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0), NOT carried on the wire. This is the fourth algorithm-agility registry, symmetric to signature-alg-registry.json, digest-suite-registry.json and mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. MLS group messages keep their own HPKE internals via mls-ciphersuite-registry.json and are out of scope here.
suite_id_grammar: suite_id = 'ak.hpke_' kem_id '_aead_' aead_id '.v' major ; each id segment matches [a-z0-9]+ . The canonical_id is the full wire string; it is NOT freely composed from parts — only suites present as rows below exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.
registry_rules: Only suites present as rows in this registry exist. Implementations MUST NOT compose KEM/KDF/AEAD ids freely; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite id not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_hpke_suite when it appears in an HPKE-sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ak.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope). Receivers MUST NOT infer suite parameters from the AEAD name alone.

Schema enum values for HPKE suite selector fields (e.g. ak.schema.key_backup.v1 encryption.hpke_suite, the ak.secret.send / member-application / file-transfer envelope `scheme` const) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

When a surface carries both an explicit `hpke_suite` selector and an AEAD `name`/profile field, the AEAD MUST equal the selected suite's aead; a mismatch MUST be rejected (schema_violation). A surface MAY omit the selector only where a single default-MUST suite is pinned by its defining document, in which case the absent selector denotes that row.

status=reserved rows pin the wire id and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_hpke_suite) on a reserved suite id seen on wire before activation.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/artifact_lint enforces this binding.

For every surface_profiles row, info_and_aad names one exact canonical byte string. The sender MUST pass those identical bytes as both RFC 9180 SetupBaseS info and the single-shot AEAD Seal aad; the receiver MUST pass the same bytes as both SetupBaseR info and AEAD Open aad. Empty, domain-only, differently wrapped, or independently serialized info/AAD values are forbidden.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new KEM families (post-quantum / hybrid), new KDFs and new AEADs enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the ak.hpke_*_aead_*.v* wire form needs no rewrite. Nonce handling is RFC 9180 key-schedule-derived, uniformly across every HPKE-sealed surface (`recovery_public_key` envelopes, the to-device `ak.secret.send` seal, member-application and file-transfer key envelopes): the AEAD nonce is base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0) and MUST NOT be carried on the wire; each seal mints a fresh ephemeral key, so base_nonce is unique per envelope. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5 for the symmetric (non-HPKE) key-backup nonce-uniqueness rules.

kem_strength_order.note: Classical KEMs are treated as equal classical strength; the hybrid xwing row is strictly stronger (adds ML-KEM-768 post-quantum confidentiality). Consumed by any future no-downgrade rule on suite transition.

suites.security_note: All-RFC-9180 suite for key-backup recovery_public_key envelopes on platforms with AES hardware acceleration. Classical.

v1 default-MUST application-layer HPKE suite: all-RFC-9180 base mode DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) + HKDF-SHA256 + 96-bit-nonce ChaCha20-Poly1305 (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR, key_schedule-derived base_nonce, no wire nonce). Software-friendly (constant-time, no AES hardware needed), the default for the recovery_public_key / to-device / member-application / file-transfer envelopes. Classical (not post-quantum).
P-256 KEM for WebAuthn/FIDO2/PKI key-agreement interop, mirroring the ECDSA-P256 signature row. Profile-gated; receivers not advertising ak.profile.hpke.p256.v1 fail closed. Classical.

suites.kat_absence_reason: The X-Wing HPKE construction remains reserved until the profile and per-suite KAT activation requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: ak.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specifies draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10 and HPKE KEM id 0x647A; any incompatible draft change requires an explicit registry release and refreshed KAT digest before activation
Per-suite HPKE conformance vectors published (KEM encap/decap, key schedule, sealed bytes)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: key-backup envelope before MLS KeyPackage (static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target; reuses the reserved ak.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace)
suites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) per the encryption-and-audit.md §2 PQ roadmap. The KEM identifier is the IANA-assigned HPKE value 0x647A and the exact construction is pinned to draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until the profile and KAT activation requirements are complete.
